title: Ampleness on algebraic spaces is etale local on the base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:F\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $M$ be a line module on $F$. On a scheme $Z$, a line module on its small etale site is identified with an ordinary invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] via the equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on the Zariski and small etale sites of $Z$; ampleness of a line module on a scheme means ampleness of this invertible module. Suppose $\{g_i:Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale maps with each $Y_i$ a scheme. Assume $F_i=F\times_YY_i$ is a scheme for every $i$, and let $M_i$ be the pullback of $M$ along the etale map $F_i\to F$. Assume that for every affine open $W\subseteq Y_i$ the restriction of $M_i$ to $F_i\times_{Y_i}W$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $f$ is representable: for every scheme $T$ and every map $h_T\to Y$, the fibre product $F\times_YT$ is a scheme. Moreover, for every scheme $T$ with an etale map $h_T\to Y$ and every affine open $W\subseteq T$, the pullback of $M$ along the etale map $F\times_YW\to F$ is ample. In particular, if $Y$ is a scheme, then $F$ is a scheme, and the restriction of $M$ to $f^{-1}(W)$ is ample for every affine open $W\subseteq Y$.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample); Divisors on Spaces, spaces-divisors.tex Tag 0D36 (lemma-relatively-ample-local), with relative ampleness as in Tag 0D31 (definition-relatively-ample). The scheme hypothesis means ampleness on inverse images of affine opens, as in Morphisms, morphisms.tex Tag 01VH (definition-relatively-ample).

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary scheme $T$ with a map $T\to Y$. Put $X=F\times_YT$, $T_i=Y_i\times_YT$, and $X_i=X\times_TT_i\simeq F_i\times_{Y_i}T_i$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $X$ is an algebraic space, and the base-changed families cover $T$ and $X$. The $T_i$ are schemes: the maps $Y_i\to Y$ are representable etale maps. Their projections to $T$ form a jointly surjective etale family, and $X_i$ is a scheme since $F_i,T_i,Y_i$ are schemes. These assertions use the scheme-test definition of etale maps of algebraic spaces in [def-trf-algebraic-space] and associativity of sheaf fibre products. Let $N_i$ be the ordinary pullback of $M_i$ to $X_i$, invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. By [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change], $N_i$ is ample on the inverse image of every affine open of $T_i$. On $X_i\times_XX_j$, pull back the restriction identifications of $M$ on $F_i\times_FF_j$. Functoriality of tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] makes these isomorphisms satisfy identity and triple-overlap cocycles. By [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent] they descend to a line module $N$ on $X$. If $T\to Y$ is etale, $N$ is canonically the restriction of $M$: that restriction has the same local identifications, and the full faithfulness in the same descent lemma glues the identity maps and their inverses.

source.place: Tag 0D36 (lemma-relatively-ample-local), reduction to scheme tests; Tag 0893 for the scheme pullback; spaces-descent.tex Tag 04W8 for the auxiliary line module on X.

proof.text: Write $f_T:X\to T$ and $f_i:X_i\to T_i$ for the projections. The forward implication of [lem-trf-scheme-ample-canonical-proj-criterion] makes each $f_i$ quasi-compact and separated, because $N_i$ is $f_i$-ample by Step 1. Now [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] applies to the cover $\{T_i\to T\}$ and gives that $f_T$ is quasi-compact and separated. This supplies the compactness and separation hypotheses needed for the section algebra; no representability of $f_T$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), paragraph beginning By Divisors on Spaces; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03KG,03KM.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-space-section-algebra-etale-base-change], $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}(f_T)_*N^{\otimes d}$ is a quasi-coherent graded algebra on the scheme $T$. Let $\psi:f_T^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}N^{\otimes d}$ be its evaluation homomorphism. The relative Proj existence theorem [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] supplies the scheme $P=\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$. Apply [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] to obtain an open $U=U(\psi)\subseteq X$ and a map $r:U\to P$. For each $i$, the section-algebra lemma identifies $\mathcal A_i=(T_i\to T)^*\mathcal A$ with $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}(f_i)_*N_i^{\otimes d}$ and identifies the restricted $\psi$ with the evaluation map $\psi_i$. In degree $d$ this is precisely the restriction comparison $(f_T)_*N^{\otimes d}|_{T_i}\simeq(f_i)_*N_i^{\otimes d}$; it sends a section to its restriction, so evaluation sends that section to the same local section of $N_i^{\otimes d}$. Thus these are the canonical maps to which the scheme ampleness criterion applies.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, section-algebra and adjunction-map paragraphs; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LX; spaces-divisors.tex Tag 0D2Z.

proof.text: For each $i$, [lem-trf-scheme-ample-canonical-proj-criterion] applies to $(f_i,N_i)$ and its canonical algebra from Step 3: it gives $U(\psi_i)=X_i$ and an open immersion $r_i:X_i\to P_i=\operatorname{Proj}_{T_i}(\mathcal A_i)$. By [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map], $U\times_TT_i=U(\psi_i)=X_i$ and $P_i\simeq P\times_TT_i$, with $r_i$ equal to the base change of $r$. The complement of $U$ is empty: the maps $X_i\to X$ cover, and its inverse image in each $X_i$ is empty. Therefore $U=X$. The maps $P\times_TT_i\to P$ are a jointly surjective etale scheme family, being base changes of $T_i\to T$; the scheme covering base-change lemma [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] verifies this. Apply [lem-trf-space-open-immersion-etale-local] to $r:X\to P$: its base changes are the open immersions $r_i$. Hence $r$ is an open immersion and $X$ is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, final paragraphs; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M4, open-immersion case.

proof.text: Regard $N$ now as an ordinary invertible module on the scheme $X$, using the scheme-site interpretation of [lem-trf-algebraic-space-invertible-descent]. The compatibility clause of [lem-trf-space-section-algebra-etale-base-change] identifies the algebra and evaluation map of Step 3 with the ordinary Zariski section algebra and evaluation map. The canonical-map comparison of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] identifies $r$ with the ordinary canonical map. Since $f_T$ is quasi-compact and separated, $U=X$, and $r$ is an open immersion, the reverse implication of [lem-trf-scheme-ample-canonical-proj-criterion] gives that $N|_{f_T^{-1}(W)}$ is ample for every affine open $W\subseteq T$. In particular $X=F\times_YT$ is a scheme for every scheme test $T\to Y$, proving representability. For an etale test $T\to Y$, Step 1 identified $N$ with the restriction of $M$, so this proves precisely the requested ampleness on every $F\times_YW$. Finally, when $Y$ is a scheme take $T=Y$ with its identity map: it is etale, and gives both that $F$ is a scheme and ampleness over every affine open of $Y$.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 0D3C, 0D35, 0D36. Kept the statement; proved its full arbitrary-scheme representability test by a section-algebra/relative-Proj argument. Seven strictly supporting lemmas are stated and searched, rather than restating affine ampleness descent as a new node. For arbitrary tests a line module is constructed by the existing invertible-descent theorem; for etale tests full faithfulness identifies it with the given restriction. All scheme comparison and base-change compatibilities used are explicit in supporting statements.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the polarized-scheme descent input in the existing historical ancestry from lem-trf-local-term-locality, specifically the sentence that the descended ample module forces the quotient to be a scheme; no trace-formula or purity route is changed.

tool_uses.why: Existence of the relative Proj scheme is a generic construction used for the section-algebra embedding; this unit supplies no alternative construction.
Generic scheme covering stability verifies the target cover on which the Proj map is an open immersion.
The generic scheme pullback theorem ensures the local line modules on arbitrary scheme tests are invertible and their tensor pullbacks compose.
